US rule (hard limit or requirement): No federal minimum age. ECOA lets the lender refuse a person without capacity to contract (state law sets the age of majority, usually 18). Age is a prohibited basis otherwise. A validated scoring model may use age, but may not give a negative value to applicants aged 62+.
No card for under-21s unless the written application shows independent ability to pay, or a cosigner aged 21+ who can pay. No limit increase before 21 unless the same test is met.

Lender MAY consider immigration / permanent-resident status (Reg B). 2023 CFPB-DOJ caution statement withdrawn 12 Jan 2026. CFPB statement of 8 Jun 2026: lenders relying on US job income may be OBLIGATED to consider immigration status where the records show income may stop. National origin is still a prohibited basis.

parameter: Max personal-loan size or income multiple
US rule (hard limit or requirement): No federal rule; left to the lender (and to state law). Reg Z covers non-mortgage consumer credit only up to $73,400 in 2026.

No DTI cap since the 2021 General QM rule (43% removed). Lender must consider AND verify DTI or residual income. QM status is decided by price: APR below APOR + 2.25 pts (first lien ≥ $137,958 in 2026), with higher spreads for smaller loans.
type: requirement + price cap for QM status

US rule (hard limit or requirement): Manual max 36%, up to 45% with credit-score and reserve conditions; DU max 50%. Investor rule, not law.

FHA manual: 31/43 base; up to 40/50 with 2 compensating factors (580+ score); scores 500-579 or no score capped at 31/43. VA: 41% benchmark plus residual-income test; above 41% needs written justification.

Lender must make a reasonable, good-faith judgement of ability to repay, using 8 verified factors (income/assets, job, payment, other loans, housing costs, debts, DTI or residual income, credit history).

Lender must consider income or assets and current debts before opening a card or raising a limit. Written policy must use DTI, debt-to-assets or residual income. No card for someone with no income or assets.
No APR or fee increase except: promo rate of at least 6 months, variable index, advance notice for NEW transactions only (not in first year), 60+ days late, workout failure, SCRA.
Each statement: "Minimum Payment Warning", payoff time and cost at minimum, 36-month payment, counselling phone number.

2024 "$8" rule VACATED (N.D. Tex., 15 Apr 2025). eCFR still prints the vacated text. Exact safe-harbor amount in force now: VERIFY (see Part C). Fees must be "reasonable and proportional" in any case. First-year fees capped at 25% of the credit limit.
Only if the consumer has opted in.
36% Military APR for active-duty members and dependents (includes most fees and add-ons). Does not apply to mortgages or vehicle-purchase loans secured by the vehicle.
No federal usury cap. A national bank may charge the rate allowed by its home state and "export" it to borrowers in other states. States set usury limits.

No federal LTV cap in Reg Z. Fannie Mae (and Freddie Mac) may not buy above 80% LTV without credit enhancement, so mortgage insurance is used. PMI can be cancelled on request at 80% and ends automatically at 78% of original value.
$832,750 (one unit); high-cost ceiling $1,249,125. 2027 figure due late Nov 2026.
APR ≥ APOR + 1.5 pts (first lien, conforming), + 2.5 (jumbo), + 3.5 (second lien) = higher-priced: escrow and appraisal rules apply; QM gets only a rebuttable presumption.
QM: term up to 30 years; no negative amortization; no interest-only; no balloon (small-creditor exception). Non-QM loans may have these features but must still pass ATR.
No federal rate, term or LTV cap found. TILA/Reg Z disclosures, ECOA, FCRA apply; MLA does not cover vehicle-purchase loans secured by the car.

Need a permissible purpose (credit transaction). Adverse action based on a report: give score, key factors, bureau details and rights. Risk-based pricing notice when terms are materially less favourable.

Prohibited bases: race, colour, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, public-assistance income, exercising consumer-credit rights. Adverse action notice within 30 days with SPECIFIC reasons. Since 21 Jul 2026 Reg B says ECOA does not create disparate-impact liability (intentional discrimination and proxies still banned). CFPB Circulars 2022-03 and 2023-03 (complex algorithms) WITHDRAWN May 2025, but the specific-reasons rule still applies.

APR must be accurate within 1/8 point (1/4 irregular). 3-business-day right to cancel on non-purchase loans secured by the home (up to 3 years if disclosures are missing). Loan Estimate within 3 business days of application; Closing Disclosure received 3 business days before closing.
Mortgages: only on fixed-rate, QM, non-HPML loans; max 2% (years 1-2), 1% (year 3), none after 3 years; must also offer a no-penalty option.
2024 interpretive rule (BNPL = credit card under Reg Z) WITHDRAWN 12 May 2025; CFPB said it will not issue a revised rule. No BNPL-specific federal rule in force; states acting (e.g., New York).

FDCPA / Reg F apply to third-party debt collectors (not usually to a bank collecting its own debt). Presumed harassment if more than 7 calls in 7 days, or a call within 7 days of a phone conversation.
CECL (ASC 326): lifetime expected loss, with reasonable and supportable forecasts. In force for all banks since fiscal years after 15 Dec 2022.

Substandard at 90 days past due; charge off closed-end at 120 days and open-end (cards) at 180 days; 1-4 family: value test and charge-off of shortfall at 180 days; bankruptcy within 60 days of notice; fraud within 90 days.

SR 11-7 / OCC 2011-12 REPLACED by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 (17 Apr 2026). Risk-based, focused on banks over $30bn; "not enforceable standards" but unsafe practices can still be cited. Covers statistical and non-generative ML models; generative and agentic AI are out of scope.
